claim: The tubular ER network has a diameter of ~30 nm in yeast.
source: The tubular endoplasmic reticulum (ER) network is a morphologically unique part of the ER that consists of interconnected cylindrical membrane structures, with a diameter of ~30 nm in yeast and ~50 nm in higher eukaryotes (Hu et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hu et al., 2011.

claim: The tubular ER network has a diameter of ~50 nm in higher eukaryotes.
source: The tubular endoplasmic reticulum (ER) network is a morphologically unique part of the ER that consists of interconnected cylindrical membrane structures, with a diameter of ~30 nm in yeast and ~50 nm in higher eukaryotes (Hu et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hu et al., 2011.

claim: Tubules in the ER network constantly form, retract, move, and fuse with one another.
source: In this network, tubules constantly form, retract, move, and fuse with one another (Du et al., 2004; Griffing, 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Du et al., 2004 and Griffing, 2010.

claim: Approximately 30% of the ER in Saccharomyces cerevisiae is composed of the tubular network.
source: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, electron microscope (EM) tomography has revealed that ~30% of the ER is composed of the tubular network (West et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to West et al., 2011.

claim: In yeast and plant cells, the tubular ER is mostly found beneath the plasma membrane in a region termed the cortical ER.
source: In yeast and plant cells, the tubular ER is mostly found beneath the plasma membrane, a region termed the cortical ER (Griffing, 2010; Prinz et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Griffing, 2010 and Prinz et al., 2000.

claim: In mammalian cells, ER tubules are frequently found in the cell periphery with a cluster of tubules in the perinuclear region.
source: In mammalian cells, ER tubules are frequently found in the cell periphery, but there is usually a cluster of tubules in the perinuclear region (Baumann and Walz, 2001; Shibata et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Baumann and Walz, 2001 and Shibata et al., 2006.

claim: ER tubules have high membrane curvature on cross section.
source: ER tubules have high membrane curvature on cross section.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript.

claim: High membrane curvature in ER tubules is generated and stabilized by reticulons (RTNs) and DP1/Yop1p.
source: Such curvature is generated and stabilized by a class of integral membrane proteins, the reticulons (RTNs) and DP1/Yop1p (Hu et al., 2008; Voeltz et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hu et al., 2008 and Voeltz et al., 2006.

claim: Deletion of reticulons and Yop1p causes a loss of tubules and a corresponding gain in sheets.
source: Deletion of these proteins causes a loss of tubules and a corresponding gain in sheets, and purified reconstituted Yop1p and Rtn1p generate tubules in vitro (Hu et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hu et al., 2008.

claim: Purified reconstituted Yop1p and Rtn1p generate tubules in vitro.
source: Deletion of these proteins causes a loss of tubules and a corresponding gain in sheets, and purified reconstituted Yop1p and Rtn1p generate tubules in vitro (Hu et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hu et al., 2008.

claim: The reticulon homology domain (RHD) is the most conserved region of tubule-forming proteins.
source: The most conserved region of these proteins is the reticulon homology domain (RHD) (Shibata et al., 2008; Voeltz et al., 2006), which contains two tandem transmembrane (TM) segments.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Shibata et al., 2008 and Voeltz et al., 2006.

claim: The RHD contains two tandem transmembrane (TM) segments.
source: The most conserved region of these proteins is the reticulon homology domain (RHD) (Shibata et al., 2008; Voeltz et al., 2006), which contains two tandem transmembrane (TM) segments.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Shibata et al., 2008 and Voeltz et al., 2006.

claim: Each TM segment in the RHD consists of 30–35 amino acids.
source: Each of these segments consists of 30–35 amino acids, which is too long to traverse the membrane once but too short to traverse it twice; therefore, they likely form transmembrane hairpins (TMHs).
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript.

claim: TM segments in the RHD likely form transmembrane hairpins (TMHs).
source: Each of these segments consists of 30–35 amino acids, which is too long to traverse the membrane once but too short to traverse it twice; therefore, they likely form transmembrane hairpins (TMHs).
evidence: The claim is based on logical inference from the length of the TM segments.

claim: Tubule-forming proteins form homo- or hetero-oligomers.
source: In addition, these tubule-forming proteins form homo- or hetero-oligomers (Shibata et al., 2008), which could serve as curved scaffolds.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Shibata et al., 2008.

claim: ER tubules can be pulled out from a flat membrane by attaching to the growing tip of the microtubule or interacting with motor proteins.
source: ER tubules can also be pulled out from a flat membrane by either attaching to the growing tip of the microtubule or interacting with motor proteins (Shibata et al., 2009; Zimmerberg and Kozlov, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Shibata et al., 2009 and Zimmerberg and Kozlov, 2006.

claim: The tip of a newly formed tubule is often marked by Rab10 in complex with phosphatidylinositol synthase (PIS) and CEPT1.
source: In these cases, the tip of a newly formed tubule is often marked by Rab10 in complex with phosphatidylinositol synthase (PIS) and CEPT1 (English and Voeltz, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to English and Voeltz, 2013.

claim: Fusion between ER tubules is mediated by atlastin (ATL), a dynamin-like GTPase.
source: Fusion between tubules is mediated by a class of dynamin-like GTPase, atlastin (ATL) (Hu and Rapoport, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hu and Rapoport, 2016.

claim: Depletion of ATL results in an unbranched ER phenotype.
source: Depletion of ATL results in an unbranched ER phenotype (Hu et al., 2009; Rismanchi et al., 2008), and purified and reconstituted Drosophila ATL fuses vesicles in vitro (Bian et al., 2011; Orso et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Hu et al., 2009 and Rismanchi et al., 2008.

claim: Purified and reconstituted Drosophila ATL fuses vesicles in vitro.
source: Depletion of ATL results in an unbranched ER phenotype (Hu et al., 2009; Rismanchi et al., 2008), and purified and reconstituted Drosophila ATL fuses vesicles in vitro (Bian et al., 2011; Orso et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bian et al., 2011 and Orso et al., 2009.

claim: Sey1p is a functional ortholog of ATL in yeast.
source: No ATL is found in yeast, but a functional ortholog, Sey1p, has been identified.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript.

claim: ATL and Sey1p are exchangeable in the maintenance of ER morphology in cells.
source: ATL and Sey1p are exchangeable in the maintenance of ER morphology in cells (Anwar et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Anwar et al., 2012.

claim: GTP binding induces dimerization in ATL and Sey1p.
source: Structural and biochemical analysis has revealed that GTP binding induces dimerization, and hydrolysis-driven conformational changes are important for the fusion by ATL and Sey1p (Bian et al., 2011; Byrnes et al., 2013; Byrnes and Sondermann, 2011; Yan et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bian et al., 2011; Byrnes et al., 2013; Byrnes and Sondermann, 2011; Yan et al., 2015.

claim: Hydrolysis-driven conformational changes are important for fusion by ATL and Sey1p.
source: Structural and biochemical analysis has revealed that GTP binding induces dimerization, and hydrolysis-driven conformational changes are important for the fusion by ATL and Sey1p (Bian et al., 2011; Byrnes et al., 2013; Byrnes and Sondermann, 2011; Yan et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Bian et al., 2011; Byrnes et al., 2013; Byrnes and Sondermann, 2011; Yan et al., 2015.

claim: ATL and Sey1p contain a TMH near the C-terminus that interacts with the RHD of tubule-forming proteins.
source: Both GTPases contain a TMH near the C-terminus that interacts with the RHD of tubule-forming proteins and facilitates the localization of these ER fusogens in the tubular ER (Hu et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hu et al., 2009.

claim: Two Rtns and one Yop1p have been identified in yeast.
source: Two Rtns and one Yop1p have been identified in yeast, and four Rtns and six REEPs (DP1 being REEP5) (Shibata et al., 2008), each with variable isoforms, have been identified in mammals.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Shibata et al., 2008.

claim: Four Rtns and six REEPs have been identified in mammals.
source: Two Rtns and one Yop1p have been identified in yeast, and four Rtns and six REEPs (DP1 being REEP5) (Shibata et al., 2008), each with variable isoforms, have been identified in mammals.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Shibata et al., 2008.

claim: Sey1p is the only well-characterized ER fusogen in yeast.
source: Sey1p is the only well-characterized ER fusogen in yeast, and three ATLs have been identified in mammals (Rismanchi et al., 2008; Zhu et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rismanchi et al., 2008 and Zhu et al., 2003.

claim: Three ATLs have been identified in mammals.
source: Sey1p is the only well-characterized ER fusogen in yeast, and three ATLs have been identified in mammals (Rismanchi et al., 2008; Zhu et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Rismanchi et al., 2008 and Zhu et al., 2003.

claim: Loss of Rtns and Yop1p in S. cerevisiae results in retarded growth.
source: Loss of Rtns and Yop1p in S. cerevisiae results in retarded growth (Voeltz et al., 2006), and in Caenorhabditis elegans it significantly decreases the embryo survival rate (Audhya et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Voeltz et al., 2006.

claim: Loss of Rtns and Yop1p in Caenorhabditis elegans significantly decreases the embryo survival rate.
source: Loss of Rtns and Yop1p in S. cerevisiae results in retarded growth (Voeltz et al., 2006), and in Caenorhabditis elegans it significantly decreases the embryo survival rate (Audhya et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Audhya et al., 2007.

claim: Deletion of Sey1p in Candida albicans results in decreased virulence.
source: Deletion of Sey1p in Candida albicans results in decreased virulence (Yamada-Okabe and Yamada-Okabe, 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Yamada-Okabe and Yamada-Okabe, 2002.

claim: Deletion or mutation of RHD3 in Arabidopsis thaliana yields short root hairs and severe growth defects.
source: Deletion or mutation of RHD3, a homolog of Sey1p in Arabidopsis thaliana, yields short root hairs and severe growth defects (Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2013.

claim: Depletion of ATL in Drosophila melanogaster and Danio rerio causes neuronal defects.
source: Furthermore, depletion of ATL in Drosophila melanogaster and Danio rerio causes neuronal defects (Fassier et al., 2010; Lee et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Fassier et al., 2010 and Lee et al., 2009.

claim: Mutations in ATL1 cause hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) in humans.
source: In humans, mutations in ATL1 cause hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP), a neurodegenerative disease (Salinas et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Salinas et al., 2008.

claim: A total of 832 proteins have been identified as ER proteins in rat liver samples.
source: A total of 832 proteins have been identified as ER proteins in rat liver samples (Gilchrist et al., 2006) and 294 proteins as microsomal proteins in Pichia pastoris (Klug et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gilchrist et al., 2006.

claim: A total of 294 proteins have been identified as microsomal proteins in Pichia pastoris.
source: A total of 832 proteins have been identified as ER proteins in rat liver samples (Gilchrist et al., 2006) and 294 proteins as microsomal proteins in Pichia pastoris (Klug et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Klug et al., 2014.

claim: Proteins important for sheet formation have been revealed by comparative analysis of rough microsomes.
source: Though proteins important for sheet formation have been revealed by comparative analysis of rough microsomes (Shibata et al., 2010), the proteome of ER tubules has yet to be reported.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Shibata et al., 2010.

claim: The study isolated tubular ER via immunoprecipitation against a tubule-specific marker.
source: Here, we isolated tubular ER via immunoprecipitation against a tubule-specific marker.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the method used in the study.

claim: Quantitative proteomic analysis revealed 79 proteins that are enriched in tubular ER.
source: Quantitative proteomic analysis by isotope-labeling mass spectrometry revealed 79 proteins that are enriched in tubular ER.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the main finding of the study.

claim: Yop1p marks the tubular ER network.
source: Yop1p marks the tubular ER network (Voeltz et al., 2006) and Sec63p, a component of the translocon-associated complex, marks the entire ER.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Voeltz et al., 2006.

claim: Sec63p marks the entire ER.
source: Yop1p marks the tubular ER network (Voeltz et al., 2006) and Sec63p, a component of the translocon-associated complex, marks the entire ER.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the manuscript.

claim: No obvious HAC1 processing or Kar2p upregulation was observed in cells expressing Yop1p and Sec63p.
source: No obvious HAC1 (an UPR-regulated transcription activator) processing or Kar2p (an ER luminal chaperone) upregulation, commonly used indicators of the UPR in yeast (Cox and Walter, 1996), was observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C and a citation to Cox and Walter, 1996.

claim: HAC1 processing and Kar2p upregulation are commonly used indicators of the UPR in yeast.
source: No obvious HAC1 (an UPR-regulated transcription activator) processing or Kar2p (an ER luminal chaperone) upregulation, commonly used indicators of the UPR in yeast (Cox and Walter, 1996), was observed (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Cox and Walter, 1996.

claim: Pma1p was largely diminished from S20K.
source: Pma1p, a proton pump localized in the plasma membrane, and porin, a mitochondrial β-barrel protein, were largely diminished from S20K.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the experiment, as shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Porin was largely diminished from S20K.
source: Pma1p, a proton pump localized in the plasma membrane, and porin, a mitochondrial β-barrel protein, were largely diminished from S20K.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the experiment, as shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A small amount of Pma1p reappeared in P100K, likely due to the tight association between the plasma membrane and cortical ER.
source: A small amount of Pma1p reappeared in P100K, likely due to the tight association between the plasma membrane and cortical ER.
evidence: This is a direct statement combining observation and speculation.

claim: Golgi-targeted Tlg2p and vacuole-bound ALP remained in S100K.
source: Surprisingly, Golgi-targeted Tlg2p and vacuole-bound ALP remained in S100K.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the experiment, as shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Some of the endosomal marker Pep12p precipitated in P100K, possibly due to an association with ER membranes or its size.
source: Some of the endosomal marker, Pep12p, precipitated in P100K, possibly due to an association with ER membranes or its size, which was similar to that of microsomal vesicles.
evidence: This is a direct statement combining observation and speculation.

claim: ER-resident proteins including Sec63p, Dpm1p, Kar2p, Sey1p, and Yop1p were found mostly in P100K.
source: ER-resident proteins, including Sec63p (integral membrane protein), Dpm1p (tail-anchored protein), Kar2p (soluble luminal protein), and Sey1p and Yop1p (known ER tubule proteins), were found mostly in P100K.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the experiment, as shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Approximately half of the Kar2p protein appeared in P100K, likely captured by sealing microsomal membranes.
source: Approximately half of the Kar2p protein appeared in P100K, likely captured by sealing microsomal membranes.
evidence: This is a direct statement combining observation and speculation.

claim: A small portion of Flag-tagged Yop1p was found in S100K.
source: Notably, a small portion of Flag-tagged Yop1p was found in S100K.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the experiment, as shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Yop1p-2xFlag was observed in some, but not all, ER fractions and peaked in fractions 3–9 on a Percoll density gradient.
source: Yop1p-2xFlag was observed in some, but not all, ER fractions (labeled by HA-tagged Sec63p) and peaked in fractions 3–9, indicating an association with low-density materials.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the experiment, as shown in Figure 2A and quantified in Figure 2B.

claim: Sec63p co-existed in Yop1p-containing samples but was enriched in later fractions (12–15) with higher densities on a Percoll density gradient.
source: In contrast, Sec63p co-existed in Yop1p-containing samples but was enriched in later fractions (12–15) with higher densities.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the experiment, as shown in Figure 2A and quantified in Figure 2B.

claim: Yop1p-containing microsomes correspond to only part of the microsomal population, probably those derived from ER tubules.
source: These results suggest that Yop1p-containing microsomes correspond to only part of the microsomal population, probably those derived from ER tubules, and are generally lighter than microsomes derived from ER sheets.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Percoll gradient data.

claim: Yop1p-containing microsomes are generally lighter than microsomes derived from ER sheets.
source: These results suggest that Yop1p-containing microsomes correspond to only part of the microsomal population, probably those derived from ER tubules, and are generally lighter than microsomes derived from ER sheets.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Percoll gradient data.

claim: Only two-thirds of the total Yop1p-2xFlag was observed in the precipitates in the absence of commonly used IP detergents.
source: The precipitation was less complete in the absence of commonly used IP detergents (like Triton X-100), as only two-thirds the total Yop1p-2xFlag was observed in the precipitates (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the experiment, as shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Some ER proteins, such as Kar2p and Sey1p, co-precipitated with Yop1p-2xFlag.
source: Some of the ER proteins, such as Kar2p and Sey1p, co-precipitated.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the experiment, as shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Proteins known to be enriched in ER sheets, represented by Sec63p, were detected in the precipitates at a much lower percentage of total protein.
source: However, proteins known to be enriched in ER sheets, represented by Sec63p, were detected in the precipitates, though at a much lower percentage of total protein.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the experiment, as shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Pep12p and Pma1p that remained in P100K were absent from the precipitates.
source: In addition, the Pep12p and Pma1p that remained in P100K were absent from the precipitates (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the experiment, as shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Elution with RapiGest is more efficient than peptide elution, yielding more than 90% of the bound proteins.
source: Elution and dissolution are more efficient with RapiGest than the peptide, yielding more than 90% of the bound proteins.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the experiment, as shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D,E.

claim: Peptide-eluted TU samples contained mostly small microsomes with occasional short tubules.
source: TO samples exhibited microsomes of various sizes (Figure 2C) with diameters ranging from 200 nm to 20 nm, whereas peptide-eluted TU samples contained mostly small microsomes with occasional short tubules (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from EM analysis, as shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The diameters of structures seen in TU were ~20–30 nm, which is consistent with the reported size of the tubular ER in yeast cells.
source: The diameters of structures seen in TU were ~20–30 nm, which is consistent with the reported size of the tubular ER in yeast cells (Bernales et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from EM analysis, as shown in Figure 2D, and supported by a citation to Bernales et al., 2006.

claim: A total of 845 proteins were identified with a quantifiable TU:TO ratio.
source: A total of 845 proteins were identified with a quantifiable TU:TO ratio, and 531 were identified with a TU:BL ratio (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the proteomic analysis results, as shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A total of 531 proteins were identified with a quantifiable TU:BL ratio.
source: A total of 845 proteins were identified with a quantifiable TU:TO ratio, and 531 were identified with a TU:BL ratio (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the proteomic analysis results, as shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The median CV% of protein ratio measurements across biological triplicates was 17.5% for proteins with TU:TO ratios.
source: Reproducibility was demonstrated by the median CV% of protein ratio measurements across biological triplicates (17.5% for proteins with TU:TO ratios and 18.5% for proteins with TU:BL ratios).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the proteomic analysis results.

claim: The median CV% of protein ratio measurements across biological triplicates was 18.5% for proteins with TU:BL ratios.
source: Reproducibility was demonstrated by the median CV% of protein ratio measurements across biological triplicates (17.5% for proteins with TU:TO ratios and 18.5% for proteins with TU:BL ratios).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the proteomic analysis results.

claim: More than 90% of the proteins with TU:TO ratios had a CV% < 30%.
source: Furthermore, >90% of the proteins with TU:TO ratios (Figure 3—source data 2-1) or TU:BL ratios (Figure 3—source data 2–2) had a CV% < 30%, indicating adequate reproducibility of our proteomic quantification.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the proteomic analysis results.

claim: More than 90% of the proteins with TU:BL ratios had a CV% < 30%.
source: Furthermore, >90% of the proteins with TU:TO ratios (Figure 3—source data 2-1) or TU:BL ratios (Figure 3—source data 2–2) had a CV% < 30%, indicating adequate reproducibility of our proteomic quantification.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the proteomic analysis results.

claim: A total of 466 proteins were quantified in both TU:TO and TU:BL comparative experiments.
source: A total of 466 proteins were quantified in both TU:TO and TU:BL comparative experiments (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the proteomic analysis results, as shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A total of 231 proteins had an average TU:TO ratio >2.0 (p<0.05).
source: To isolate candidates for the tubular ER, we retained 231 proteins with an average TU:TO ratio >2.0 (p<0.05).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the proteomic analysis results.

claim: A total of 48 proteins had an average TU:TO ratio >2 (p<0.05) and TU:BL ratio >2.0 (p<0.05), which are assumed to be specifically enriched in ER tubules.
source: The list was then narrowed down to 48 proteins with an average TU:TO ratio >2 (p<0.05) and TU:BL ratio >2.0 (p<0.05), which are assumed to be specifically enriched in ER tubules (Figure 3C,D and Figure 3—source data 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the proteomic analysis results, as shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: A total of 31 proteins had an average TU:TO ratio >2.0 (p<0.05) and TU:BL ratio >1.4 (p<0.1) and are candidates for likely being enriched in ER tubules.
source: In addition, 31 proteins with an average TU:TO ratio >2.0 (p<0.05) and TU:BL ratio >1.4 (p<0.1) are candidates for likely being enriched in ER tubules (Figure 3—source data 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the proteomic analysis results.

claim: Several proteins, such as Yop1p, Rtn1p, Rtn2p, and Sey1p, are known to have important roles in forming the tubular ER network.
source: Among the 79 candidates, several proteins, such as Yop1p, Rtn1p, Rtn2p, and Sey1p, are known to have important roles in forming the tubular ER network.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on established knowledge.

claim: Half of the proteins from the inventory of 79 candidates are known to localize to the ER.
source: Half of the proteins from this inventory are known to localize to the ER, confirming the specificity of the isolation.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on database search and manual curation.

claim: Functional classification of the 79 candidates revealed that popular categories include vesicular transport and ER organization, organelle contact, lipid metabolism, signaling/stress sensing, and protein folding/degradation.
source: Functional classification of this protein inventory revealed that popular categories include vesicular transport and ER organization, organelle contact, lipid metabolism, signaling/stress sensing, and protein folding/degradation (Figure 3D and Figure 3—source data 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the functional classification results, as shown in Figure 3D.

claim: HT008 (homolog of Nvj2p/YPR091C) mostly aligned with calreticulin but was largely missing from Climp63-positive regions when over-expressed in COS-7 cells.
source: When HT008 (homolog of Nvj2p/YPR091C) and NSDHL (homolog of Erg26p) were over-expressed, they mostly aligned with calreticulin (Figure 4A,C) but were largely missing from Climp63-positive regions (Figure 4A,C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from immunofluorescence experiments, as shown in Figure 4A.

claim: NSDHL (homolog of Erg26p) mostly aligned with calreticulin but was largely missing from Climp63-positive regions when over-expressed in COS-7 cells.
source: When HT008 (homolog of Nvj2p/YPR091C) and NSDHL (homolog of Erg26p) were over-expressed, they mostly aligned with calreticulin (Figure 4A,C) but were largely missing from Climp63-positive regions (Figure 4A,C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from immunofluorescence experiments, as shown in Figure 4C.

claim: HT008 and NSDHL are enriched in ER tubules.
source: These results suggest that HT008 and NSDHL are enriched in ER tubules.
evidence: This is an inference based on the immunofluorescence data.

claim: VAPA (Scs2p) and FDFT1 (Erg9p) exhibited a similar distribution to HT008 and NSDHL when tested in COS-7 cells.
source: A similar distribution was observed when VAPA (Scs2p) or FDFT1 (Erg9p) was tested (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from immunofluorescence experiments, as shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: DPM1 and EMC2 were diffused in the cytosol but exhibited some ER association.
source: As expected, DPM1 and EMC2 were diffused in the cytosol but exhibited some ER association (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B,C).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from immunofluorescence experiments, as shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B,C.

claim: All tested candidate proteins were found in the P100k fraction, suggesting that they co-purified with the ER.
source: All tested proteins were found in the P100k fraction (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A,B), suggesting that they co-purified with the ER.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from microsome preparation experiments, as shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Tested candidate proteins were enriched in REEP5-labeled precipitates.
source: As predicted and similar to REEP5, the tested proteins were enriched in the precipitates.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from immunoprecipitation experiments, as shown in Figure 4B,D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D,E.

claim: Climp63 was barely detected in REEP5-labeled precipitates.
source: In contrast, Climp63 was barely detected in the precipitates, and calnexin, an ER-bound chaperone, only partially co-precipitated with tubular microsomes (Figure 4B,D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from immunoprecipitation experiments, as shown in Figure 4B,D.

claim: Calnexin only partially co-precipitated with tubular microsomes.
source: In contrast, Climp63 was barely detected in the precipitates, and calnexin, an ER-bound chaperone, only partially co-precipitated with tubular microsomes (Figure 4B,D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from immunoprecipitation experiments, as shown in Figure 4B,D.

claim: Endogenous HT008, NSDHL, and VAPA were found in P100K and enriched in REEP5-Flag-labeled precipitates.
source: Endogenous HT008, NSDHL, and VAPA were found in P100K (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C) and enriched in REEP5-Flag-labeled precipitates (Figure 4—figure supplement 3D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from experiments using a Flp-In-293 cell line expressing REEP5-Flag, as shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3C,D.

claim: YPR091C (recently annotated as Nvj2p) and YDL121C appeared as an ER pattern with little co-localization with other markers when expressed in COS-7 cells.
source: YPR091C (recently annotated as Nvj2p) and YDL121C were predicted to be membrane proteins and appeared as an ER pattern with little co-localization with other markers.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from immunofluorescence experiments, as shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4A,B.

claim: YMR209C was found in the ER when expressed in COS-7 cells.
source: YMR209C contained a potential signal peptide and was found in the ER.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from immunofluorescence experiments, as shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4C.

claim: YNL208W was predicted to be cytosolic but exhibited some ER association when expressed in COS-7 cells.
source: YNL208W was predicted to be cytosolic but exhibited some ER association (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from immunofluorescence experiments, as shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4D.

claim: COS-7 cells failed to express YBL086C.
source: In contrast, COS-7 cells failed to express YBL086C.
evidence: This is a direct statement of an observation from the experiments.

claim: The tubular ER network may be involved in membrane trafficking, lipid metabolism, organelle contact, and stress sensing.
source: Functional categorization of the list of proteins revealed that the tubular ER network may be involved in membrane trafficking, lipid metabolism, organelle contact, and stress sensing.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on functional categorization of the identified proteins.

claim: Affinity isolation coupled with quantitative proteomics is a useful tool for investigating ER functions.
source: We propose that affinity isolation coupled with quantitative proteomics is a useful tool for investigating ER functions.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the authors' proposal based on their study.

claim: Curvature-sensitive functions or localization are expected for ER tubule-enriched proteins.
source: A unique feature of ER tubules compared to the rest of the ER is that it adopts high membrane curvature on its cross-section. Thus, curvature-sensitive functions or localization are expected for ER tubule-enriched proteins.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on logical inference from the structural properties of ER tubules.

claim: In yeast cells, most of the COPII vesicles form in the tubular ER.
source: In yeast cells, most of the COPII vesicles, which transport cargo from the ER to Golgi, form in the tubular ER (Okamoto et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Okamoto et al., 2012.

claim: Pex30p has been shown to contain a RHD, which is composed of two tandem TMHs.
source: Pex30p has consistently been shown to contain a RHD, which is composed of two tandem TMHs; it is capable of tubulating membranes and may play a role in PPV biogenesis (Joshi et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Joshi et al., 2016.

claim: Pex30p is capable of tubulating membranes and may play a role in PPV biogenesis.
source: Pex30p has consistently been shown to contain a RHD, which is composed of two tandem TMHs; it is capable of tubulating membranes and may play a role in PPV biogenesis (Joshi et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Joshi et al., 2016.

claim: Tubule-shaping proteins play roles in the nuclear envelope (NE) reassembly after mitosis.
source: Tubule-shaping proteins play roles in the nuclear envelope (NE) reassembly after mitosis (Dawson et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Dawson et al., 2009.

claim: The membranes surrounding the nuclear pore have high curvature similar to that of ER tubules.
source: Furthermore, the membranes surrounding the nuclear pore have high curvature similar to that of ER tubules (Mészáros et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Mészáros et al., 2015.

claim: POM33 has been implicated in the nuclear pore complex distribution and NE remodeling.
source: POM33 (TU:TO 3.81; TU:BL 3.79) may provide additional linkage between nucleus biogenesis and ER tubules, as it has also been implicated in the nuclear pore complex distribution and NE remodeling (Casey et al., 2015; Chadrin et al., 2010; Floch et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Casey et al., 2015; Chadrin et al., 2010; Floch et al., 2015.

claim: Components of the p24 family complex, Erp2p and Erv25p, along with Erp1p and Emp24p, sort GPI-anchored proteins into COPII vesicles.
source: Components of the p24 family complex, Erp2p (TU:TO 3.12; TU:BL 2.88) and Erv25p (TU:TO 3.93; TU:BL 2.93), along with Erp1p (not included in our list, but with TU:TO 1.39, TU:BL 1.79, p<0.05) and Emp24p, sort GPI-anchored proteins into COPII vesicles (Belden and Barlowe, 2001; D'Arcangelo et al., 2015; Schröder et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Belden and Barlowe, 2001; D'Arcangelo et al., 2015; Schröder et al., 1995.

claim: Emp47p functions in glycoprotein secretion.
source: Emp47p (TU:TO 2.58; TU:BL 2.19), a yeast homolog of ERGIC-53, functions in glycoprotein secretion (Sato and Nakano, 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sato and Nakano, 2002.

claim: Pho86p and Pho88p are required for the export of phosphate transporter Pho84p.
source: Pho86p (TU:TO 2.49; TU:BL 3.21) and Pho88p (TU:TO 5.68; TU:BL 3.24) are required for the export of phosphate transporter Pho84p (James and Nachiappan, 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to James and Nachiappan, 2014.

claim: ER tubules make extensive contacts with other membranes, including the plasma membrane (PM), mitochondria, and endosomes.
source: ER tubules have been shown to make extensive contacts with other membranes, including the plasma membrane (PM), mitochondria, and endosomes (Creutz et al., 2004; Du et al., 2011; Giordano et al., 2013; Kornmann et al., 2009; Toulmay and Prinz, 2012; West et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Creutz et al., 2004; Du et al., 2011; Giordano et al., 2013; Kornmann et al., 2009; Toulmay and Prinz, 2012; West et al., 2011.

claim: Tricalbin proteins Tcb1p, Tcb2p, and Tcb3p are homologs of extended synaptotagmins in mammals, which localize in the ER and associate with the PM.
source: Tricalbin proteins Tcb1p (TU:TO 2.49; TU:BL 1.57), Tcb2p (TU:TO 3.30; TU:BL 1.72), and Tcb3p (TU:TO 2.37; TU:BL 3.40) are homologs of extended synaptotagmins in mammals, which localize in the ER and associate with the PM (Toulmay and Prinz, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Toulmay and Prinz, 2012.

claim: Scs2p is known for ER-PM contact.
source: Scs2p (TU:TO 4.01; TU:BL 3.19), a homolog of VAP-A, is also known for ER-PM contact (Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kim et al., 2015.

claim: YPR091C was renamed Nvj2p for its localization between the nucleus and vacuole.
source: It was renamed Nvj2p for its localization between the nucleus and vacuole (Toulmay and Prinz, 2012) and was recently found to form an inducible contact with Golgi (Liu et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Toulmay and Prinz, 2012.

claim: Nvj2p was recently found to form an inducible contact with Golgi.
source: It was renamed Nvj2p for its localization between the nucleus and vacuole (Toulmay and Prinz, 2012) and was recently found to form an inducible contact with Golgi (Liu et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2017.

claim: Erg9p (squalene synthase) acts in the earlier steps of ergosterol biogenesis.
source: Erg9p (TU:TO 4.60; TU:BL 2.57), or squalene synthase, acts in the earlier steps (Jennings et al., 1991), whereas Erg26p (TU:TO 3.61; TU:BL 3.34) and Erg27p (TU:TO 4.28; TU:BL 1.58) play roles in the later steps (Gachotte et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Jennings et al., 1991.

claim: Erg26p and Erg27p play roles in the later steps of ergosterol biogenesis.
source: Erg9p (TU:TO 4.60; TU:BL 2.57), or squalene synthase, acts in the earlier steps (Jennings et al., 1991), whereas Erg26p (TU:TO 3.61; TU:BL 3.34) and Erg27p (TU:TO 4.28; TU:BL 1.58) play roles in the later steps (Gachotte et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gachotte et al., 1998.

claim: Members of the conserved ER membrane protein complex (EMC) including EMC1, EMC2, and EMC4 were identified as ER tubule-enriched proteins.
source: Members of the conserved ER membrane protein complex (EMC) were also identified, including EMC1 (TU:TO 3.19; TU:BL 2.07), EMC2 (TU:TO 2.73; TU:BL 1.84), and EMC4 (TU:TO 2.34; TU:BL 1.58), the function of which are yet to be identified but likely related to lipid synthesis and/or transfer (Lahiri et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the proteomic analysis results.

claim: The function of EMC proteins are yet to be identified but likely related to lipid synthesis and/or transfer.
source: Members of the conserved ER membrane protein complex (EMC) were also identified, including EMC1 (TU:TO 3.19; TU:BL 2.07), EMC2 (TU:TO 2.73; TU:BL 1.84), and EMC4 (TU:TO 2.34; TU:BL 1.58), the function of which are yet to be identified but likely related to lipid synthesis and/or transfer (Lahiri et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Lahiri et al., 2014.

claim: Yet1p and Yet3p physically interact with Scs2p and the transcriptional repressor Opi1p.
source: Yet1p (TU:TO 2.44; TU:BL 2.67) and Yet3p (TU:TO 2.42; TU:BL 2.74) physically interact with Scs2p and the transcriptional repressor Opi1p (Wilson et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wilson et al., 2011.

claim: The Yet1p-Yet3p-Scs2p-Opi1p complex plays a key regulatory role during inositol starvation.
source: The resulting complex plays a key regulatory role during inositol starvation.
evidence: This is a direct statement based on established knowledge.

claim: ER stress was reported to be sensed and alleviated by Nvj2p.
source: Recently, ER stress was reported to be sensed and alleviated by Nvj2p (Liu et al., 2017), an ER tubule-enriched protein, as shown here.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2017.

claim: The ER-mitochondria contact is mainly mediated by the ER mitochondrial encounter structure (ERMES) complex.
source: For example, the ER-mitochondria contact is mainly mediated by the ER mitochondrial encounter structure (ERMES) complex (Kornmann et al., 2009) and occurs predominantly in ER tubules (Friedman and Voeltz, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Kornmann et al., 2009.

claim: The ER-mitochondria contact occurs predominantly in ER tubules.
source: For example, the ER-mitochondria contact is mainly mediated by the ER mitochondrial encounter structure (ERMES) complex (Kornmann et al., 2009) and occurs predominantly in ER tubules (Friedman and Voeltz, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Friedman and Voeltz, 2011.
